issues.legal_issue: An ex-parte decree should be set aside when the defendant establishes a genuine and sufficient reason for absence on the hearing date and applies promptly, even if earlier negligence is alleged.
material_facts: A suit for rent, eviction and damages was decreed ex parte after neither the defendant nor his lawyer appeared on the hearing date.
The defendant said that illness while he was away for work prevented him from returning to court, and that his lawyer could not attend because the lawyer’s nephew died in an accident that day.
The defendant supported his application with an affidavit and medical certificate and applied within the statutory period.
The defendant had raised a substantive defence to the suit.
The lower courts rejected the application, including because the medical certificate was from a private doctor and because of the defendant’s previous conduct.
issues.conclusion: The absence was supported by sufficient cause, and the application should have been allowed. The ex-parte decree and the lower courts’ orders were set aside on payment of costs, with the defendant given an opportunity to prove his case.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an ex-parte decree may be set aside if summons were not duly served or if sufficient cause prevented the defendant from appearing when the suit was called for hearing. Sufficient cause is an elastic expression to be construed liberally in light of the circumstances of each case, particularly where the absence was not negligent or intentional. The relevant cause concerns the date on which the ex-parte proceedings began; prior negligence that was overlooked or condoned does not defeat an application if sufficient cause for absence on that date is shown. A prompt application and absence that was not mala fide or intentional normally support exercising discretion in the defendant’s favour, and the other party may be compensated by costs. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: ex_parte_decree_challenge and (defendant_absence_due_to_illness_or_work_emergency or counsel_absence_due_to_family_emergency) and prompt_application and absence_not_intentional

predicates.ex_parte_decree_challenge: The proceeding challenges a decree made after the defendant did not appear when the suit was called for hearing.
predicates.defendant_absence_due_to_illness_or_work: The defendant was unable to attend because illness or a work-related emergency prevented attendance.
predicates.counsel_absence_due_to_family_emergency: The defendant’s lawyer was unable to attend because of a family emergency.
predicates.prompt_application: The defendant applied to set aside the decree within the applicable statutory period.
predicates.absence_not_intentional: The defendant’s absence was not deliberate or mala fide.

issues.definition: When a challenge to an ex-parte decree involves a prompt application and a non-intentional absence explained by illness, a work emergency, or the lawyer’s family emergency, the decree is set aside on appropriate terms.
